newsitem.title: USA: Chase Manhattan keeping eye on M&A market.
newsitem.headline: Chase Manhattan keeping eye on M&A market.

text.p: A Chase Manhattan Corp spokeswoman on Thursday confirmed that the company's chairman and chief executive, Walter Shipley, discussed acquisition possiblities in a meeting with analysts the previous day.
But Shipley also told the meeting that Chase had its hands full with integrating systems and processes from the merger of the old Chase with Chemical Banking Corp, the spokeswoman said.
Shipley's comments came in response to questions, she said.

One analyst in a research memo issued on Thursday wrote that Shipley had discussed the acquisition issue, saying Chase was monitoring the situation closely and was prepared to take advantage of opportunites.
The analyst, Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman, said Shipley at one stage "pointedly mentioned the Bank of New York Co Inc -State Street Boston Corp situation as one he is watching."
On January 2, Bank of New York said it had accumulated a 4.99 percent stake in State Street Boston and was seeking approval to raise the stake to 9.9 percent.
The spokeswoman said the Bank of New York stock position in State Street had been mentioned, but she disagreed with the view that it was a pointed reference.
She said the gist of Shipley's comments on acquisitions was that Chase was looking at the market with interest but it was still hard at work completing its own post-merger integration.

The spokeswoman said Shipley observed that if the company bought an equities underwriting firm it would face a difficult integration because of the difference in cultures between an investment bank and a commercial bank.
On another topic, the spokeswoman said Shipley said the credit card business continued to be competitive but it was still a good business.
